newsitem.title: UK: FX IN EUROPE- DLR SEEKS DIRECTION AFTER BUBA NEWS.
newsitem.headline: FX IN EUROPE- DLR SEEKS DIRECTION AFTER BUBA NEWS.

text.p: The dollar made up some more lost ground in European trading but lacked the momentum to stay above 1.87 marks after an initial rally on the Bundesbank's announcement of another fixed rate repo tender, dealers said.
The sluggish dollar tone persisted across the board, with dollar/yen hovering around 116 yen and dollar/Swiss franc stuck ahead of 1.53 francs.
Intense speculation about a move higher in German rates had eased in the past days and few dealers expected to see a rise or a switch to variable tenders at today's money market operations.

But since the Bundesbank only set one tender and made no further announcement, markets are likely to keep speculating about German rates, traders said. The Bundesbank council meets again on August 21 after a four-week recess.
"After next week's council meeting the probability of a move should rise again," said Kay Sinden, economist at Bankers Trust.

Sinden said the effective easing of monetary conditions due to the mark's weaknesss and its inflationary implications as well as tentative signs that the domestic economy is recovery, were likely to make the case for higher German rates more convincing.

The U.S. unit rallied about half a pfennig after the Bundesbank set this week's repo tender at an unchanged and fixed 3.00 percent. But it ran into resistance just above 1.87 and quickly more than reversed its gains.
At 1500 GMT the dollar was at 1.8620/30 marks and 115.90/116.00 yen compared with 1.8545/55 and 115.75/80 in late European trading on Monday.

With U.S. economic fundamentals still working in favour of a higher dollar, many traders see the U.S. unit retesting its near-eight year high of just above 1.89 marks to eye 1.90 in the next week or two but said it looked set for consolidation in the near-term.

U.S. July retail sales and producer price data on Wednesday and the July consumer price index and industrial production figures on Thursday will provide the next focus for the market. The performance of U.S. asset markets is also being closely watched after Friday's sell-off amid fears of rising inflationary pressures.
Dealers said the market was reluctant to build up long dollar positions against the yen after Friday's four-yen decline and seemed content with consolidating around the 116 yen level.

Sterling was unimpressed by higher-than-expected UK July inflation data. The headline inflation rate hit a two-year high of 3.3 percent, up from 2.9 percent in June, mainly due to one-off effects such as a rise in petrol prices and increased housing costs after a series of rate rises.
Traders said the market was on hold ahead of the Bank of England's quarterly inflation report on Wednesday and data on unemployment and average earnings.
The BOE report has added significance because it is the first since the central bank's monetary policy committee assumed responsibility for setting interest rates.
"We might get a more hawkish tone than the market is expecting," said Thomas Rayner, international economist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull in London said.
Sterling was at 2.9362/72 marks, down from 2.9470/80 marks. Against the dollar, it was at $1.5772/80 from $1.5898/08.
The Australian dollar weakened slightly in response to comments from Royal Bank of Australia governor Ian Macfarlane, traders said.

Macfarlane said it was appropriate that Australian interest rates were lower than in the U.S. The economy could safely grow 4.5 percent or more over the next few years without having a detrimental effect on inflation.
He did not give a clue about the future direction of rates but said lower rates directly benefited Australian businesses.
The Australian dollar was at US$0.7376/81 from $0.7391/96 at the close in Sydney. -- Astrid Zweynert London newsroom + 44 171 542 7792
